findings.statement: CXCR2 leads the convergence ranking, with expression, replication across cohorts, genetics, literature and tractability (several CXCR1 and CXCR2 antagonists in clinical development) all contributing.

Higher baseline CXCR2 is associated with ustekinumab non-response, but it also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders, so it marks severity rather than a ustekinumab-specific mechanism. Ustekinumab BH padj was [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6] and placebo BH padj was [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126].

CXCL8 is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders, but the placebo arm shows the same direction, so this is a severity signal. Ustekinumab BH padj was [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102] and UNIFI placebo BH padj was [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0154]. Golimumab, infliximab and vedolizumab arms did not survive correction.

In the adalimumab single-cell atlas (GSE282122, a small cohort of remitters and non-remitters), CXCL8 showed no baseline difference between remitters and non-remitters in any cell state. It changed after treatment in some states, for example a decrease in cycling mononuclear phagocytes with BH padj [gene=CXCL8; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.1.padj=0.0253].

OSM is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]). The UNIFI placebo arm is not significant (BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]), but the drug-versus-placebo interaction is not significant either (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.974]), so drug specificity is not shown. The golimumab arm did not survive correction.

TREM1 is associated with ustekinumab non-response (BH padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) but also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders (BH padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]), consistent with a general severity marker. Other biologic arms did not survive correction.

IL11 is associated with ustekinumab non-response (BH padj [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=3.68e-8]), but UNIFI placebo non-responders also differ (BH padj [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0133]), so it again points to severity.

Negative result: baseline IL23A is not associated with ustekinumab response (BH padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]), so expression of an IL-23 subunit does not stratify response to ustekinumab, which blocks IL-23 through its IL12B (p40) subunit.
Negative result: baseline ITGB7 is flat for vedolizumab response (BH padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]).

The PROGENy TNFa pathway is higher in non-responders to ustekinumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) and also in infliximab, vedolizumab, golimumab and UNIFI placebo arms, so it is a general severity axis. It is not significant in PURSUIT placebo (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]) or in the PROTECT mesalazine arm (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.5-ASA (PROTECT).padj=0.414]).

The TGFb pathway is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]) and in UNIFI placebo non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00984]), so it is not drug-specific.

JAK-STAT pathway activity is higher in non-responders for ustekinumab, infliximab and PROTECT corticosteroids, but not for golimumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.204]), so the signal does not hold across all anti-TNF cohorts.

CHRDL2 is a first-in-class opportunity that is up in cohorts [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=7]. Its transcripts are stromal, mostly inflammatory fibroblasts, with the stromal lineage agreeing in other atlases [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; other_atlases_agreeing=3] (Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026, GSE282122). The composition verdict is partly composition and an antibody is the predicted modality. Missing: any response-association data or functional validation.

CPXM1 is stromal in Smillie 2019, Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122, but Gubatan 2026 assigns it to the epithelial lineage. The discovery screen labels it partly composition and an antibody-tractable first-in-class opportunity, so part of its increase may reflect fibroblast expansion. Missing: genetics and response data.

LAX1 passes the screen but its lineage does not replicate. Smillie 2019 and GSE282122 call it T/NK, while Garrido-Trigo 2023 and Gubatan 2026 call it plasma. It is largely immune-cell derived and partly composition, so it is more a marker of infiltrating lymphocytes and plasma cells than a tissue change.

XKR9 is classed as intrinsic by the composition filter, with an epithelial lineage replicated in Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122 (not Garrido-Trigo 2023, which calls it plasma). Evidence is thin, with elevation in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=4] cohorts and low expression in each epithelial cluster. Missing: response data and functional evidence.

GLT1D1 is classed as composition-driven and its transcripts are mostly neutrophil-derived, so it reflects neutrophil infiltration rather than an intrinsic tissue change. It should be treated as a weak target despite its first-in-class label.

caveats: Response cohorts are small outside UNIFI (golimumab, infliximab, vedolizumab, etrolizumab, ACT1), so null results there are underpowered rather than evidence of absence.
Drug-versus-placebo interactions were not significant for the genes checked, so ustekinumab-specific mechanisms are not demonstrated.
The anti-TNF single-cell atlas has few patients: leads only.
Discovery candidates are mostly partly composition-driven; 'first-in-class' reflects filters, not validated dependency.

Not run: treatment_response for TNF, CXCR1 and other ranked genes, antitnf_singlecell for most genes, or celltype_expression for the CXCR1/2 axis. Convergence-ranking numbers are not quoted since no verified field path was available.
